note: Attacker-controlled raw input bytes are written to a temporary config file at /tmp/libfuzzer.<pid>.
The config file is parsed by Fluent Bit's parser configuration loader, which reads [PARSER] sections and extracts the 'regex' property value.
The regex pattern string is extracted from the config file section. The pattern ends with a raw 0xF0 byte (4-byte UTF-8 lead byte) at the end of the pattern buffer.
The regex string is passed to flb_parser_create, which eventually calls flb_regex_create to compile the pattern.
The regex pattern string is passed to str_to_regex for compilation with Onigmo.

code: ret = onig_new(reg, (const unsigned char *)start, (const unsigned char *)end, ONIG_OPTION_DEFAULT, ONIG_ENCODING_UTF8, ONIG_SYNTAX_RUBY, &einfo);
note: onig_new is called with the pattern buffer. The 'end' pointer is pattern + strlen(pattern), pointing to the null terminator. The pattern's last character is a raw 0xF0 byte (4-byte UTF-8 lead).
The pattern and its end pointer are passed to the parser. The pattern buffer ends with byte 0xF0 at position end-1.
Parsing begins with p pointing to the start of the pattern and end pointing to the end of the pattern buffer.
parse_regexp calls parse_branch to parse the pattern branch, passing the pattern pointer and end pointer.
parse_branch calls parse_exp to parse each expression in the branch. The pointer p is advanced through the pattern.
parse_exp calls fetch_token to get the next token. At this point, *src points to the last byte of the pattern (0xF0 at position end-1).
PEND checks p < end. Since p is at end-1, PEND is false, so parsing continues.
PFETCH is invoked on the last byte 0xF0. The macro calls ONIGENC_MBC_TO_CODE(enc, p, end) which calls mbc_to_code, then advances p by enclen(enc, p, end).
Reads byte 0xF0 at position end-1. This is a 4-byte UTF-8 lead byte. p advances to end. Since p == e, mbc_enc_len returns ONIGENC_CONSTRUCT_MBCLEN_NEEDMORE(3).
mbc_enc_len returned NEEDMORE(3). onigenc_mbclen_approximate computes (end - p) + 3 = 1 + 3 = 4, so enclen returns 4.
PFETCH advances p by 4 bytes from position end-1, so p now points to end+3, which is 3 bytes past the end of the pattern buffer.
fetch_token sets *src = p = end+3, which is 3 bytes past the end of the heap-allocated pattern buffer.
The token is classified as TK_STRING since 0xF0 is not a special regex character. tok->backp points to the 0xF0 byte at end-1.
onig_node_str_cat is called with s = tok->backp (at end-1) and end = *src (at end+3). The function will copy end - s = 4 bytes starting from end-1, reading 3 bytes past the heap buffer.

onig_strcpy is called with src = end-1 and end = end+3. It computes len = end - src = 4 and calls xmemcpy(dest, src, 4), reading 3 bytes past the heap-allocated pattern buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ 3.
